description: Identifies that the AdapterModule protocol's adapter_params() method is genuinely polymorphic and would accept prefix tuning unchanged, BUT that the rest of the PEFT plumbing (substring filter, merge utility, recipe wiring, HF PEFT export) is LoRA-shape-coupled. Frames the tension as 'one polymorphic seam + many LoRA-string-matched seams', not just 'add a new module'.
rationale: The core architectural insight. A weak answer treats it as 'add a class that implements adapter_params()'; a strong answer sees that the protocol is one of seven cooperating pieces and the other six are LoRA-coupled.

description: Identifies the substring-based adapter_key_filter ('lora' in x or 'magnitude' in x) AND identifies AT LEAST THREE places it is duplicated (get_adapter_state_dict, _get_lora_modules, validate_missing_and_unexpected_for_lora, or the _is_dora sniff in recipes, or equivalent). Names this as the structural bug to fix before adding a third adapter type.
rationale: The substring filter is the load-bearing LoRA assumption baked across the codebase. Identifying it alone is necessary; identifying the duplication count is what shows the answerer traced its blast radius.

description: Identifies that MultiHeadAttention.forward (modules/attention.py around lines 262-292) has no extension point for K/V augmentation: k_proj/v_proj produce K and V, which are consumed by _attention_call without ever being exposed to a hook or adapter. Articulates that prefix tuning requires either modifying MultiHeadAttention or wrapping it.
rationale: Locates the actual code-level wall that prefix tuning hits. A weak answer hand-waves about 'add a hook somewhere'; a strong answer reads attention.py and identifies that K/V are not exposed.

description: Engages with the attachment-point design question by explicitly considering at least two of: (a) modifying MultiHeadAttention with an optional kwarg, (b) wrapping at TransformerSelfAttentionLayer, (c) forward_pre_hook on attention, (d) subclassing MultiHeadAttention. Recommends one with a code-grounded justification.
rationale: First of five Hard-band design forks. Strong answers don't just pick one; they compare and justify. Naming only one option is not sufficient.

description: Engages with the position-embedding / RoPE design question: do prefix tokens get RoPE applied? At what positions? Articulates that RoPE is applied per-token by absolute position index (referencing position_embeddings.py), and proposes either (a) prefix tokens at positions [0, prefix_len) with real tokens shifted, (b) prefix tokens special-cased outside the position space, or (c) explicitly defers/disables RoPE on prefix with rationale.
rationale: Second design fork. Reproducibly missed across both Run 1 and Run 2. This is the strongest sequence-level discriminator: a Hard answer must engage; a Medium answer never raises the question.

description: Engages with the KV-cache design question by comparing AT LEAST TWO alternatives: (a) pre-fill the cache at setup_caches time and shift cache_pos to start at prefix_len, vs (b) regenerate / concatenate prefix to K/V on every forward, leaving the cache untouched. Articulates the memory-vs-compute tradeoff explicitly.
rationale: Third design fork. Requires reading kv_cache.py and reasoning about lifetime of the prefix. Picking one option without comparison is partial credit at best.

description: Engages with the sequence-packing implication: PackedDataset (torchtune/datasets/_packed.py) resets position IDs per-sample so they start at 0; prefix tokens that shift the per-sample sequence start break this assumption. Either proposes a concrete resolution (e.g., bake prefix offset into position-ID generation) OR explicitly disables sample packing for prefix tuning with rationale.
rationale: Fourth design fork. Reproducibly missed. Strong answers connect the model-side change to the dataset-side assumption; weak answers stop at the model boundary.

description: Engages with loss masking for prefix tokens: prefix tokens are not real data and should not contribute to the training loss. Identifies where in the recipe (or loss module) the mask gate lives and proposes how it must change.
rationale: Fifth design fork. Reproducibly missed. A Hard answer notices that 'sequence length seen by the model now includes prefix tokens' has loss-side implications.

description: Proposes a mechanism that honors the no-implementation-inheritance policy: composition, Protocols, dataclasses, optional kwargs, or free functions. Does NOT propose a base class for MultiHeadAttention, recipes, or adapter types as the unification mechanism.
rationale: Policy compliance. recipe_interfaces.py:13-19 is explicit. A proposal that violates this is non-mergeable regardless of technical correctness.

description: Identifies that get_merged_lora_ckpt is called unconditionally in the checkpoint client whenever an adapter_config is present, AND articulates that prefix tuning has no meaningful 'merge with base weights' (the prefix is part of the forward, not a delta on W). Proposes gating the call by adapter type or making it conditional on a mergeable property.
rationale: Connects two facts: the unconditional call site, and the structural impossibility of merging prefix tuning. Strong answers identify both; weak answers stop at one.

description: Names torchtune/modules/peft/_utils.py as the file containing the AdapterModule protocol, get_adapter_params, get_adapter_state_dict, and the substring filter.
rationale: Locates the central PEFT abstraction file. Required for any code-grounded plan.

description: Names BOTH LoRALinear (torchtune/modules/peft/lora.py) and DoRALinear (torchtune/modules/peft/dora.py) as the existing AdapterModule implementations, AND identifies that both wrap nn.Linear (prefix tuning structurally does not).
rationale: Required to articulate the 'shape mismatch' between existing adapters and prefix tuning.

description: Names MultiHeadAttention (torchtune/modules/attention.py) AND TransformerSelfAttentionLayer (torchtune/modules/transformer.py) as the two candidate attachment surfaces for prefix tuning.
rationale: Both attachment points must be named for the design-fork comparison to make sense.

description: Names KVCache (torchtune/modules/kv_cache.py) AND identifies its fixed pre-allocated shape (batch, num_kv_heads, max_seq_len, head_dim) or its cache_pos tracking as the relevant constraint.
rationale: Required to articulate the pre-fill vs regenerate design fork.

description: Names recipes/lora_finetune_distributed.py (or recipes/lora_finetune_single_device.py) as the recipe template to copy-paste-modify under the no-implementation-inheritance policy, AND notes that two new recipes are needed (single-device + distributed) rather than folding into existing ones.
rationale: Required to demonstrate awareness of the recipe-duplication policy as it applies here.

description: Names torchtune/models/convert_weights.py (specifically tune_to_peft_adapter_weights and/or tune_to_peft_adapter_config) as the HuggingFace PEFT export path that is LoRA-specific and would need either a new conversion path or an explicit skip for prefix tuning.
rationale: Required to articulate the HF PEFT export incompatibility. Greppable but specific enough that weak answers miss it.

description: Names torchtune/generation/_generation.py (or the generation loop / setup_caches path) AND identifies that prefix vectors must be present at every decode step during inference, not just during training.
rationale: Connects the training-side adapter to the inference-side generation path. Reproducibly missed by Run 2; required to demonstrate end-to-end thinking.

description: Identifies the ~35 sites of `adapter_cls = DoRALinear if use_dora else LoRALinear` (or equivalent) across model component builders as a separate friction point that does NOT scale to a third adapter class, and proposes a post-construction attachment path that bypasses it.
rationale: Senior-contributor depth: cross-family pattern recognition. Both runs underweighted this.

description: Identifies the `hasattr(m, 'initialize_dora_magnitude')` (or equivalent) pattern in the recipe as the existing convention for 'adapter needs a per-type post-load initialization step', and proposes following the same pattern for prefix-tuning's initialization (e.g., zero-init, Gaussian, or Li & Liang reparameterization).
rationale: Repo-native pattern reuse. Demonstrates the answerer read the recipe's model-setup block carefully.

description: Names HuggingFace PEFT's actual PrefixTuningConfig schema (peft_type: 'PREFIX_TUNING' and/or num_virtual_tokens) and notes that the current torchtune-to-HF conversion path is LoRA-only.
rationale: Shows the answerer knows the external-facing standard exists, even if it's deferred.

description: Identifies that the prefix K/V must be in [batch, num_kv_heads, prefix_len, head_dim] shape and concatenated BEFORE the GQA expand to num_heads (attention.py around lines 287-290), otherwise memory is wasted by a factor of q_per_kv.
rationale: Subtle GQA semantics. Only Run 1 caught this. Strong micro-discriminator.

description: Identifies that flex attention's BlockMask (torchtune/modules/attention_utils.py) cannot be cleanly mutated to add prefix columns, AND proposes a concrete resolution (e.g., construct BlockMask including prefix from the start, or disable flex attention when prefix tuning is on).
rationale: Specific code-level constraint on the mask side. Strong signal of deep reading.

description: Identifies the FSDP × small-per-layer-parameter interaction: prefix tensors are small relative to layer weights, the sharding policy shards on TransformerSelfAttentionLayer boundaries, and the meta-init + to_empty path requires the new module to implement to_empty (with DoRALinear.to_empty cited as the template).
rationale: Distributed correctness consideration. Run 1 raised this as honest uncertainty; only senior contributors do that.

description: Proposes a sequenced PR plan with at least three discrete PRs: (1) refactor the shared PEFT abstractions, (2) add the attention-side hook or surgical change, (3) ship the prefix-tuning module + builder + recipes + configs. Explicitly does NOT bundle the refactor with the feature.
rationale: Senior contributors land structural changes ahead of feature PRs for reviewability. Anti-bundling is a positive signal.

description: Answer is structured (e.g., TL;DR / current contract / what breaks / design forks / implementation plan / files-touched) rather than prose-only or a flat enumeration.
rationale: Hard-band answers carry enough material to need structure.

description: Cites at least 10 distinct file:line references throughout the answer, not just file names.
rationale: Senior contributors ground claims at the line level.

description: Proposes an implementation-inheritance base class for MultiHeadAttention, TransformerSelfAttentionLayer, recipes, or adapter types as the unification mechanism.
rationale: Directly violates the no-implementation-inheritance policy. Non-mergeable.

description: Claims that minimizing code duplication is a torchtune design goal, or treats recipe duplication as a defect to be refactored away as part of this PR.
rationale: Directly contradicts recipe_interfaces.py:18-19. The policy endorses duplication.

description: Proposes naming the prefix-tuning parameters with 'lora' or 'magnitude' substrings (e.g., lora_prefix_k) to satisfy the existing substring filter without refactoring it.
rationale: Smuggles a third adapter type into the LoRA naming convention. Leaves worse archaeology debt for the next contributor. Anti-pattern explicitly called out by Run 2 as Path A's bad move.

description: Proposes extending get_merged_lora_ckpt to handle prefix tuning as if it were a residual-on-Linear update, or otherwise treats prefix vectors as mergeable into base weights.
rationale: Prefix tuning is fundamentally not a residual-on-Linear update. Conflating them shows the answerer didn't internalize the structural difference.

description: Proposes editing the ~35 model-builder if/else sites manually (extending `adapter_cls = ... if ... else ...` to a three-way or larger branch) instead of using post-construction attachment / optional kwarg injection.
rationale: The if/else pattern does not scale to N adapter types. Recommending more of the same pattern is anti-Hard.

description: Claims that the checkpointer classes themselves (FullModelHFCheckpointer, FullModelTorchTuneCheckpointer, FullModelMetaCheckpointer) need editing for prefix tuning.
rationale: The checkpointer classes are mostly adapter-agnostic; the friction is in _checkpoint_client.py call sites and convert_weights.py conversion helpers, not the checkpointer class internals.

description: Recommends bundling the PEFT-abstraction refactor (substring filter generalization, get_merged_lora_ckpt gating, etc.) with the prefix-tuning feature in a single PR rather than landing them as sequenced PRs.
rationale: CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly limits generalization. A senior contributor scopes the refactor and the feature separately even when both are required.

description: Recommends 'follow the existing pattern' or 'mirror the LoRA recipe' without naming the specific pattern, file, or function being mirrored.
rationale: Hand-wavy generic-design advice. A Hard-band answer must point at the specific code the proposal is grounded in.
